Horus. The falcon-headed god of the sky and the rightful heir to Egypt's throne. Born to Isis after his father Osiris's death, Horus was conceived after Osiris had already been murdered. Horus defeated his uncle Set in a legendary and violent conflict that lasted years, ultimately claiming the throne and uniting Egypt under legitimate rule. Every pharaoh was called the Horus of their time, embodying Horus's kingship and legitimizing their divine right to rule. His falcon head and piercing eyes represented his dominion over the sky and his watchful protection of the realm. During his battle with Set, one of his eyes, the Wedjat Eye, was torn out. But it was restored, and the Wedjat Eye became a powerful protective amulet used throughout Egypt. Associated with the sky and the sun, Horus was sometimes depicted as a child being nursed by Isis or as a grown warrior. In some contexts, he was worshipped as a solar deity, merging aspects with Ra's identity as the journey of the sun. His major cult center was at Edfu, where a vast temple preserved the myth of his triumph over Set. Thoth served as judge and mediator in disputes between Horus and Set, maintaining balance and justice during their conflict. Through Horus, the concept of legitimate kingship was eternally renewed, as every pharaoh after him claimed descent from him as the rightful king of Egypt.
